assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Table columns represent the method's public inputs and observable outputs, not internal state
assertions.evidence: Columns: 'Scenario | Applicant Type | Age | Claim Count | Status? | Premium?' — no internal fields

assertions.text: No column is named after private fields or internal variables
assertions.evidence: No 'riskScore' or 'hasActivePolicy' column present in any @TableTest header

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language
assertions.evidence: 'Applicant Type', 'Age', 'Claim Count', 'Status?', 'Premium?' are business terms

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes
assertions.evidence: 'Renewal, no claims, would otherwise be standard', 'Risk score exactly at threshold'

assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Premium?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Status?, Premium?, Status?, Premium?, Premium?

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 3 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 3 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Multiple tables address distinct concerns, not one monolithic table
assertions.evidence: Three methods: autoApprovesRenewalsWithNoClaims, rejectsApplicationsAboveRiskThreshold, calculatesPremiumByAgeTier

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: Tables contain 4 rows each, targeted at distinct scenarios per concern

assertions.text: Decision logic and premium calculation are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: Method 1 and 2 assert both 'Status?' and 'Premium?': 'assertEquals(premium, result.premium(), 0.001);'

assertions.text: Test method body does not recompute internal formulas
assertions.evidence: 'EvaluationResult result = evaluator.evaluateApplication(...); assertEquals(status, result.decision());' — no arithmetic in body

assertions.text: @Description explains business context, not internal formulas
assertions.evidence: 'Risk score is age/10 + claimCount * 15. Applications are rejected once the score exceeds 75.'

assertions.text: Approval decision table covers 4 vs 5 claims cliff across varying ages, not senior threshold
assertions.evidence: Uses 'age 9' and 'age 10' with 5 claims to hit risk score 75/76 instead of the 4-vs-5 claim cliff across ages

assertions.text: Approved premium table covers boundary effects: the premium jump from 0 to 1 claim (impact of +15 risk score on premium), and the premium difference at age 64 vs 65 (standard vs senior formula). These boundary conditions document how premium changes at each threshold.
assertions.evidence: calculatesPremiumByAgeTier rows: 64/1->142.00, 65/1->273.50, 30/0->106.00, 90/0->231.50 - no same-age 0-vs-1 claim pair; description says 'rows 3-4 vary age further with no claims'

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Status? varies per row e.g. 'AUTO_APPROVED...APPROVED...APPROVED' and Premium? varies '0.00...136.00...106.00'; no table has a constant expectation or verbatim-copy input

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: Description states 'Risk score is age/10 + claimCount * 15. Applications are rejected once the score exceeds 75' and 'Approved applicants are charged 100 + riskScore * 2.0 below age 65, and 200 + riskScore * 3.5 from age 65 onward'

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or the method name it falls back to) states what the code under test does, not an external fact it depends on.
assertions.evidence: Method names 'autoApprovesRenewalsWithNoClaims', 'rejectsApplicationsAboveRiskThreshold', 'calculatesPremiumByAgeTier' describe the method's action, not a bare domain fact

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: The generated tests pass when executed against InsuranceEvaluator
assertions.evidence: Tests passed

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, and which the table holds constant for every row, must be visible as a column or named in the @DisplayName/@Description as deliberately held fixed.
assertions.evidence: 'Applicant type does not affect premium (see the auto-approval and rejection tables for its effects), so it is held fixed at NEW here.'

assertions.text: A comparison criterion applied by the assertion must be stated on the published surface — the table, the @DisplayName, or the @Description.
assertions.evidence: assertEquals(premium, result.premium(), 0.001) is a plain equality with conventional floating-point epsilon; assertEquals(status, result.decision()) is plain equality
